title: tzap: a verified optimizer’s performance journey
summary:
Six implementation commits made the Lean CLI 1.7–10.4× faster on completed original-baseline cases. QFT now finishes in 2.14 seconds, while the original executable reaches the 60-second limit. Rust remains 16–121× faster. The fresh final comparison validates identical outputs; each earlier experiment retains its own control and decision.

This report reuses the 2026-09-10 evidence. It runs no benchmarks. Start with the baseline and directly measured totals, then inspect individual improvements and rejected ownership experiments. Timings and samples are noisy; hashes, generated code and proof contracts provide different kinds of evidence.

comparisons.title: 1–2. Array tags and cached samples · gf64
comparisons.boundary: Native CLI launch through parsing, optimization, reporting, checked serialization, file write and exit
comparisons.cohort: -O1; CPU 2; synthesis tables unused; fresh OS entropy
comparisons.identity: 2c29be4 → 447d06f + 88eb89f; binaries 068b6058 → ea8e0ac5; Lean 4.33.1; Lake release; mathlib 0df444a; AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, CPU 2; shared machine
comparisons.note:
List indexing and prefix reconstruction were visible in the original gf64 self profile. Array indexing removed those paths; generated C releases the old state before mutation. The simulation invariant relates array entries to the symbolic list. A second profile identified repeated packing of bit-function samples. Preparing a finite array once, before capturing it in the lookup closure, is selected by a proved csimp equality. The ideal randomized model remains unchanged.

The earlier array-only screen was unpinned and inconclusive on Chebyshev. This final paired result measures the two changes together, not an isolated timing claim for each commit. One warmup per binary; six AB/BA pairs on CPU 2. Every run’s four output metrics agree and the final retained QASM pair is identical. Batch Lean build and the relevant proof/test modules passed. Changes are compared within this campaign; times are not combined with other campaigns.
comparisons.decision: Accepted together; controlled comparison covers both commits

comparisons.title: 3. Verified Hadamard sweeps · chebyshev
comparisons.boundary: Native CLI launch through parsing, optimization, reporting, checked serialization, file write and exit
comparisons.cohort: -O1; CPU 2; synthesis tables unused; fresh OS entropy
comparisons.identity: 737667f → 32fbf9e; binaries ea8e0ac5 → 0a9b8398; Lean 4.33.1; Lake release; mathlib 0df444a; AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, CPU 2; shared machine
comparisons.note:
The old driver restarted a whole-list search after each rewrite. A right-to-left sweep now applies several verified rewrites, with a change flag for length-preserving rules. The existing semantic, operand-range and well-formedness contracts are preserved. An initial single-rewrite check avoids allocating a full sweep for an already irreducible circuit.

The earlier always-sweep candidate was rejected after a noisy but persistent gf64 slowdown. For QFT, the accepted candidate had six completed runs with a 6.368 s median versus a reused 60-second baseline timeout. That result is censored and is not included as a paired comparison here. One warmup per binary; six AB/BA pairs on CPU 2. Every run’s four output metrics agree and the final retained QASM pair is identical. Batch Lean build and the relevant proof/test modules passed. Changes are compared within this campaign; times are not combined with other campaigns.
comparisons.decision: Accepted: resolves QFT timeout; Chebyshev improves; arithmetic broadly flat

comparisons.title: 4. Pass packed entropy directly · qft20
comparisons.boundary: Native CLI launch through parsing, optimization, reporting, checked serialization, file write and exit
comparisons.cohort: -O1; CPU 2; synthesis tables unused; fresh OS entropy
comparisons.identity: 32fbf9e → 7628452; binaries 0a9b8398 → 6c11e592; Lean 4.33.1; Lake release; mathlib 0df444a; AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, CPU 2; shared machine
comparisons.note:
The runner already reads random words, but exposed them through bit functions before packing them again. It now normalizes the owned word array once and captures it for indexed lookup. Proofs establish the word/bit/word identity, masking and zero-padding behavior, and equality of IO actions including errors. The high-bit and partial-width guards pass.

A rejected function-returning helper was eta-expanded: normalization moved into every lookup. Adding inline did not solve that code shape. Returning the prepared array before creating the closure did. Generated C confirms the placement; the final QFT self profile no longer samples bitsToWordAux. Profile percentages describe separate noisy captures, not exact allocation counts. One warmup per binary; six AB/BA pairs on CPU 2. Every run’s four output metrics agree and the final retained QASM pair is identical. Batch Lean build and the relevant proof/test modules passed. Changes are compared within this campaign; times are not combined with other campaigns.
comparisons.decision: Accepted: removes redundant conversion with IO equality

comparisons.note: Unconditional composition previously used the conditional combinator with an always-true predicate. The equality theorem preserves IO behavior, and generated C confirms the changed ownership. The measured effect is mostly neutral; fewer retained owners alone do not establish a runtime win. The old fixpoint constructor eagerly built a pass/name chain for the entire fuel budget. The direct runner constructs only rounds that execute. Generated C has a tail-loop back edge. The original circuit remains owned during the post-pass length comparison. runFixpointShrink_eq proves equality of the IO action; tests check zero fuel, exhaustion, equal-length changed results, convergence, and error/effect counts.

Ten alternating AB/BA pairs were collected because the expected effect was small. gf32 stays flat; gf64 has a 2.7% lower median, but only six of ten pairs improve and its mean changes little. comparisons.decision: Accepted direct loop; incremental runtime benefit is small and noisy

attribution.title: A full application boundary
attribution.text:
All headline observations include process startup, parsing, optimization, normal reporting, serialization, output writing and exit. Lean also reparses its output to check the round trip. Rust is explicitly sequential. O3 synthesis caches are already populated, but loading them is inside the measured command. Fresh 128-bit tags come from OS entropy. These are application timings, not a controlled comparison of language overhead.

We have not measured a complete phase-duration breakdown. Self-profile symbols identify costs to investigate; they do not justify assigning seconds to startup, parsing, optimization or shutdown.

attribution.title: From asymptotic scans to preparation placement
attribution.text: Array tags removed repeated list indexing and prefix reconstruction. Caching finite samples removed repeated packing. Hadamard sweeps removed whole-list restarts after each successful rewrite. Finally, keeping sampled entropy packed removed an unnecessary word/bit/word round trip. Each source change has its corresponding invariant or equivalence proof. The rejected eta-expanded helper illustrates why generated C, rather than source placement alone, mattered.

attribution.title: Linearity was a mechanism question, not a promised speedup
attribution.text:
The tag-state mutator already exposed an exclusive array update after releasing its parent. Unconditional composition removed another owner. Releasing gate wrappers and retaining only a count in fixpoint iteration also changed ownership as intended, but did not improve the representative results. Those candidates were rejected. The accepted fixpoint loop removes eager pass construction while preserving the prior ownership during the length comparison.

The earlier always-sweep Hadamard candidate and eta-expanded sample helper are documented as rejected designs in the archived reports and patches; they are not mixed into accepted distributions.

attribution.title: What the profiles can support
attribution.text:
Early DWARF chains had impossible callers, so inclusive flamegraphs were discarded. The bundled viewers display self instruction-pointer weights from the intended native executables. They are instrumented runs separate from the acceptance timing distributions. The old QFT profile is a 60-second prefix; the later profiles complete the CLI, so their phase mixes differ. No synthetic chronology or Perfetto timeline is presented.

After the accepted changes, allocation, list scans and O3 table loading remain useful targets to attribute. A small array-copy percentage does not prove that all ownership costs are negligible.

attribution.title: Correctness and identity
attribution.text: The final branch passed a batch Lake build, including affected proof modules and regression guards. Beam was used for speculative checks without replacing those builds with saved server checkpoints. The final suite has 162 invocations: 161 successes and the single original QFT timeout. All successful output files match within their workload and independent scans reproduce gate counts, two-qubit counts, T-counts and depth. Earlier campaigns validate each run’s reported metrics and the final retained QASM pair; their runners reused output paths, so they do not preserve a distinct QASM file for every historical run.

Each completed series has six measured runs; every retained output agrees within its case. The earlier selected rows compare each experiment with its own control. They are not a cumulative curve and their savings must not be added or multiplied. Rejected trials remain visible.
